_note: E7 deepfake-voice CEO attack fragment (wave 4). A fragment of the `social` block; the full-episode shell copies these keys into scenarios/awareness_e7_*/scenario.json.erb, and the defend-only/check shells leave the attack out. E7 is the optional cross-role finale (`11` A1, `11` §3.2 E7 row), reuses E1's Brightwell Foods cast (BRAND_SET.md `brightwell_foods`: 'E7 reuses E1 emails'), and HAS NO ATTACK SCORE (`scored: false`, like E1/E3/E5, and additionally checklist-only, never judged on audio realism). The learner, a junior red-teamer on an authorised Brightwell exercise, prepares the fictional script for a cloned-voice call that impersonates the chief executive Ravinder Sandhu and pressures the accounts-payable clerk (phish target `ceo_voice_target` = Tom Reilly) to release an urgent supplier payment. No real person's voice is used; the TTS 'clone' is a style variant of an in-world voice (`11` §3.2 note, held P7-Z1/Z2). The lesson is 'verify, don't trust the ear': voice alone is not proof. See 'Globals the shell must declare' and 'Open design questions' below.

Unscored and checklist-only.

brightwell_ceo.text: Ravinder Sandhu is Brightwell Foods' chief executive and often speaks at food-industry events.
brightwell_ceo.subject: ravinder
brightwell_ceo.reduceNote: Recordings of a leader speaking in public are the raw material for a cloned voice; the voice is no longer private once it is on a conference stage.

brightwell_ceo_travel.text: Ravinder Sandhu posted that he is away in Leeds this week visiting a supplier site, with a packed schedule.
brightwell_ceo_travel.subject: ravinder
brightwell_ceo_travel.reduceNote: A post that puts a leader out of the office with no time to talk gives a caller a believable reason to be rushed and hard to reach back.

brightwell_payments_clerk.text: Tom Reilly in accounts payable releases Brightwell's supplier payments.
brightwell_payments_clerk.subject: tom
brightwell_payments_clerk.reduceNote: Naming the person who actually releases payments tells an attacker exactly whom to call, not just whom to email.

brightwell_open_payment.text: Quarter-end note: a large supplier payment is due to go out this week once it is signed off.
brightwell_open_payment.subject: tom

provides.label: the supplier payment due this week

brightwell_open_payment.reduceNote: A known pending payment lets a caller name the exact thing they want pushed through, so the request sounds like business as usual.

greet_rushed.text: Tom, it's me, I've only got a minute between site visits.

pretext_ceo_payment.text: I need {payment} pushed through today while I'm off-site. It's signed off at my end, I just can't get to a desk to do it myself.

pretext_catchup.text: Just checking the month-end numbers are on track before I'm back.

ask_pay_now.text: Release it today, and keep it between us until I'm back and can explain.

seededMessages.subject: Authorised exercise: Brightwell Foods (finale)
seededMessages.body:
Hello,

This is the Brightwell Foods finale. In scope: this inbox and the people on it. Research what's public about the chief executive, then write one short message: the email in his name that would go with a cloned-voice call. No real person is used, nothing leaves this account, and you are not scored on how convincing it is.

Red team lead

blocks.text: Quarter-end: a large supplier payment is due to go out this week once it is signed off.

posts.text: In Leeds all week visiting sites, back to back, so bear with me on email. Good to see the teams up here.
Twenty-five years of the chilled range this month. Proud of the whole team.

primedFor.story: a rushed call that sounds like the chief executive, pushing a payment he can explain later

open.fail: Nothing about the caller or the reason made him act on it.

senderTrust.pass: ✓ It sounds like the chief executive he knows
senderTrust.fail: He does not place this voice as the chief executive, so a rushed payment request carries no weight.
senderTrust.redFlag: The From line carries Ravinder Sandhu's real Brightwell address, so it reads as the chief executive, but it was forged: Ravinder never sent it, and a From line can be set to show any name and address.

pretextRelevant.pass: ✓ Ties to a payment he is already expecting to release
pretextRelevant.fail: No payment he can match this to, so no reason to act on it.

urgencyCalibrated.fail: 'Release it today, and keep it between us' leaves no time to check and no one to check with, which is the pressure that works here.
urgencyCalibrated.redFlag: The 'today, and keep it between us' line leaves no time to check and no one to ask.

replies.landed: Of course, I'll release it now and keep it quiet until you're back.
replies.missed: I'm not releasing that off a message. I'll ring Ravinder on the number we hold and confirm before anything moves.

hints: Whose voice would a clerk in accounts payable act on without a second thought?
What payment is already due this week, so the request sounds like normal business?
Name the chief executive and tie the call to the payment on file; the rush then does the rest.

_openDesignQuestions._note: E7 is optional (`11` A1) and its runner/schema support is not scheduled. Flagged for the wave-4 runner and validator owners.
_openDesignQuestions.voiceScriptStage: The write beat is framed (C2-M4) as the email in the CEO's name that would go with a cloned-voice call, authored here on the write/mail surface, because the runner plays no audio and the learner only ever writes a message. A dedicated voice-script surface (and flip playback of a clip) would be cleaner but needs a runner stage and schema that do not exist. Modelled as mail write so it validates against the existing phishTargets schema.
_openDesignQuestions.flipPlayback: The E7 flip would replay the script as audio (vo7_ceo_clone) rather than render an email; audio is held (P7-Z2), so the flip stays transcript-only and the runner's mail-based flip view is the stand-in.
_openDesignQuestions.noAttackScore: scored:false matches E1/E3/E5; E7 adds 'never judged on audio realism' and 'checklist only' (`11` §3.2). No extra scoring field is needed because the attack beat is unscored in every episode.
